content.study:
Scienter liability historically concerns harm caused by an animal where the keeper knew of a dangerous propensity and failed to control it. Modern Indian claims must also be tested against negligence and applicable animal-control statutes.\
\
The common-law scienter action distinguishes ordinary animal behaviour from a known vicious or dangerous tendency. Knowledge is central. Indian courts may apply common-law principles where consistent with Indian law, while negligence may provide a separate route where the keeper failed to take reasonable care.
